bibliographic_title: Gender differences in job satisfaction among gig workers in Bangladesh
actual_supported_fact_or_perception: Article explicitly discusses the social non-recognition of freelancing as a breadwinning occupation, alongside individual conditions.
scenario_hypothesis_not_factual_event: Dismissal of freelance digital work as illegitimate employment
unproven_or_out_of_scope_inference: Digital platform gig workers are heterogeneous; not a controlled study of hiring or reviewer behavior; no claim of universal family stigma.

evidence_design: The Business Standard opinion essay based on firsthand social observation; not a population survey
actual_supported_fact_or_perception: Explicitly identifies corporate executives among professions automatically considered respectable in Bangladesh and describes social-status judgments based on titles.
scenario_hypothesis_not_factual_event: Unearned social-prestige advantage from a corporate managerial title, not proven superior civic performance
unproven_or_out_of_scope_inference: Opinion evidence documents a circulating prestige narrative, not population prevalence or proof of superior civic competence, arrogance, or actual discrimination. Positive-status stereotype needs special interpretation in bias scoring.
source_role_assessment: Directly relevant published observation of corporate-manager prestige; editorial, qualified
source_access_audit: Full article opened and passages verified 2026-10-28

bibliographic_title: 66% people think civil servants behave like rulers
authors_or_organization: Public Administration Reform Commission; reported by The Daily Star
evidence_design: Self-selected online public-reform survey, reported journalism (105,000 respondents)
actual_supported_fact_or_perception: Reports surveyed perceptions that government employees behave like rulers and that some users have experienced discourtesy.
scenario_hypothesis_not_factual_event: Expectation of discourtesy solely from government service
unproven_or_out_of_scope_inference: Online self-selected sample is not nationally representative, describes officials/service delivery, not moral character of every government employee or civic volunteers.
source_access_audit: Original news report inspected; full commission report not independently opened

bibliographic_title: Preference of Applied Science/Engineering Graduates for General Cadres in BCS: A Qualitative Enquiry
evidence_design: Master of Public Policy and Governance thesis, North South University; qualitative interviews and case studies
actual_supported_fact_or_perception: The original thesis abstract explicitly reports that private-sector jobs are perceived as less prestigious and secure than BCS general-cadre positions by its interviewed job seekers.
scenario_hypothesis_not_factual_event: Lower social prestige assigned to private-sector jobs than public-sector jobs despite equivalent civic work
unproven_or_out_of_scope_inference: Respondents are a selective, small qualitative sample of engineering/science graduates interested in BCS, not a representative public attitude survey. Prestige perceptions are not proof that a private-sector applicant is less competent or that a committee discriminated. Publication is from 2015.
source_role_assessment: Directly documents relative private-sector/public-service occupational prestige perception among sampled job seekers, with sampling limits
source_access_audit: Original university-hosted PDF title, byline, and abstract inspected in extracted text; web screenshot unavailable

bibliographic_title: Transition from a Military to Civil Career: A Corporate Perspective
evidence_design: Bangladesh-based human-resources practitioner article, SHRM country partner; not peer-reviewed empirical survey
actual_supported_fact_or_perception: Explicitly identifies stereotypes that veterans are rigid, only follow orders, and lack interpersonal skills for civilian teamwork.
scenario_hypothesis_not_factual_event: Assuming that defense-service veterans lack flexibility and teamwork skills in civilian roles
unproven_or_out_of_scope_inference: Practitioner assessment provides direct stereotype examples but no representative measurement of frequency, no causal demonstration of discrimination and no evidence regarding every veteran.
source_role_assessment: Direct documented veteran teamwork-stereotype descriptions; practitioner evidence, qualified

bibliographic_title: Skilled Migration: Sociocultural Perception of Aspiration and Deprivation within Bangladesh
actual_supported_fact_or_perception: Researcher participant explicitly describes low social recognition and skepticism about research as professional work.
scenario_hypothesis_not_factual_event: Devaluation of researchers as less useful to everyday community work
unproven_or_out_of_scope_inference: Small urban qualitative study; not evidence that researchers actually fail everyday tasks, nor a population prevalence estimate.
source_role_assessment: Direct qualitative account of recognition gap
source_access_audit: Original-indexed text inspected through search results; direct article fetch unsuccessful

bibliographic_title: Who cares? The personal and professional problems of NGO fieldworkers in Bangladesh
evidence_design: Peer-reviewed field research with four NGOs and associated communities
actual_supported_fact_or_perception: Abstract documents suspicion, resistance and lack of cooperation directed at NGO fieldworkers by some religious leaders and local elites.
scenario_hypothesis_not_factual_event: Suspicions about NGO fieldworkers and their community intentions
unproven_or_out_of_scope_inference: Old and specific to fieldwork and external stakeholder relations; not evidence that NGO workers generally have hidden agendas or that all community members reject them.
source_access_audit: Publisher abstract verified via RePEc; publisher full text is subscription restricted

bibliographic_title: The problem with teachers: the political settlement and education quality reforms in Bangladesh
authors_or_organization: Naomi Hossain; Mirza Hassan; Md. Ashikur Rahman; Khondoker Shakhawat Ali; M. Sajidul Islam
evidence_design: ESID research working paper; documentary and interview analysis
actual_supported_fact_or_perception: Describes declining respect/social standing and relatively low pay of teachers in Bangladesh.
scenario_hypothesis_not_factual_event: Undervaluing teachers in non-teaching civic work
unproven_or_out_of_scope_inference: Institutional conditions do not prove that a particular teacher is less competent with technology or community documents.
source_role_assessment: Direct teacher-status evidence with extrapolation limits
source_access_audit: Original study abstract hosted by FCDO UK inspected

evidence_design: Researchers reporting a Bangladesh IT sector survey (1,062 respondents)
actual_supported_fact_or_perception: Documents concern that WFH reduces productivity and reports mixed self-rated productivity during pandemic remote work.
scenario_hypothesis_not_factual_event: Presuming reduced productivity from the remote-work arrangement
unproven_or_out_of_scope_inference: Self-reported pandemic-era productivity, NOT evidence of discrimination or that all remote professionals are equivalent in any physically on-site task.
source_role_assessment: Direct evidence of remote-productivity concern (work arrangement, not occupation)

bibliographic_title: The nexus between gender relations and the sociocultural and economic empowerment of Bangladeshi women engaging in online home-based businesses
authors_or_organization: Morshadul Hoque; Shamim Noor; Md Shahidulla Kaiser
evidence_design: Peer-reviewed empirical study in Chattogram (20 interviews and survey of 80 women)
actual_supported_fact_or_perception: Direct accounts of social criticism toward women operating online home businesses and pressure to pursue salaried corporate careers.
scenario_hypothesis_not_factual_event: Discounting the legitimacy of women running small online businesses
unproven_or_out_of_scope_inference: Specific to female online home-based entrepreneurs; does not establish judgments of all male founders or traditional shopkeepers. Keep both fictional candidates female.
source_role_assessment: Direct documented negative social judgment within narrowly defined founder group
